chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Mukhtar ibn Ziyad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man has one hundred and ninety dirhams and thirty-nine dinars; should he pay zakat on them? He said: 'No, there is no zakat upon him in the dirhams nor in the dinars until forty dinars are completed and the dirhams amount to two hundred.'

I said: And a man has four camels, thirty-three sheep, and twenty-six cows; should he pay zakat on them? He said: 'He does not pay zakat on any of them because none of the categories have been completed, so zakat is not obligatory upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the minimum thresholds (nisab) for zakat on gold, silver, and livestock in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the precise nisab thresholds for various forms of wealth, emphasizing that the obligation of zakat is triggered only when the complete minimum quantity is possessed, not merely approached. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that partial holdings do not incur liability, a principle that underpins the Shia jurisprudence of wealth purification. This ruling ensures that zakat remains a manageable burden, reflecting the divine mercy in Islamic economic law.
